title: THE SAVOY MALE AND FEMALE COLLEGE
text:
The two Whitworth committeewomen have ceased acquaintances, it would have been a good guard to make in secrecy. As a new committee man, editor may not be aware of the background of my touch with the Jones and King family of "Ginger Joe" and of others who have lived here. An interesting reminiscent mention of them was made in my home, and I stayed awhile in Jim Jones' drug store when rather small. My recollection is very distinct and clear about a professional visit by. King made in my home. As to the King family affair, but I can go this one better. I was listening to a conversation between Dr. K. and my father. In the discussion was the stone of the church across the street of "Come Argel Road," the observation was made, that if it were a window, so much the better. My father, and I heard him, remarked that: "Were a band of angels to really appear, there would not be a window sash left in the building!" The speaker's graphic description of the fancy built a vast scene of the results and in later years there is not a window intact! In memory, I was shocked at the visions of the little pickaxinettes as many appeared to be present. As a businessman now, I am no less realistic, and I hope the visions went with me down to old age. Even now my voice is very weak and faltering.

"Lord I care not for riches, neither silver nor gold," and I do not find himself in trouble while he held the fold.

"I would make sure of Heaven, I would enter the fold."

With a background like that I should not be surprised at almost anything but it also ended with a vision of the youth in those days that would hold "Mag." Anyway, the members of the committee are free to act as they see fit. I have told you of the ideas that I have put in the way of the affair. The object before the committee is the really important thing and earth-bound policies and a banquet might inhibit wise deliberations of the committee.

I am in receipt of your (Mac Ed's letter in which he listens your letter to him and I certainly appreciate his thoughts about the matter and I am very much as you stated the same feeling about the way you handled the matter and the keen interest

**Letter to the Reunion Committee from Mr. E. A. McMahon, Dallas, Texas, December 4, 1937.
